topics: F. F. Blackman's Law of Limiting Factors (1905)

CO2 Saturation Points ($C_4 \approx 360\ \mu\text{L/L}$ vs $C_3 \approx 450\ \mu\text{L/L}$) & CO2 Fertilization Effect

quickSummary: Blackman's Law of Limiting Factors (1905) states that the rate of a multi-variable biological process is governed by the factor present at the lowest level. Light saturates at 10% of full sunlight; at low light, light is limiting. CO2 is the chief limiting factor in nature (0.03-0.04%). C4 plants saturate at ~360 μL/L CO2 with a compensation point of 0-10 μL/L; C3 plants saturate at ~450 μL/L CO2 with a compensation point of 40-100 μL/L, allowing greenhouse CO2 enrichment. C4 plants possess higher temperature optima (30-45°C) than C3 plants (20-25°C).

summaryBox.takeaway: The rate is determined by the factor closest to its minimum. Light saturates at 10% sunlight. CO2 is the chief natural limiter (C4 saturates at 360 μL/L, C3 at 450 μL/L).

conceptBreakdown.content: *"When a biological process is conditioned as to its rapidity by a number of separate factors, the rate of the process is limited by the pace of the slowest factor."*

conceptBreakdown.heading: 9.1 Major Environmental Factors & Critical Thresholds
conceptBreakdown.title: 9.1 Major Environmental Factors & Critical Thresholds
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Light Intensity**:
   - **Light Compensation Point**: Intensity where photosynthetic $\text{CO}_2$ uptake equals respiratory $\text{CO}_2$ output (Net gas exchange $= 0$).
   - **Light Saturation Point**: Occurs at **$10\%$ of full sunlight**. Beyond this, further light increases do not boost photosynthesis and can cause chlorophyll photo-oxidation (solarization).
2. **$\text{CO}_2$ Concentration (Chief Limiting Factor in Nature)**:
   - **Compensation Point**: $C_3 = 40\text{--}100\ \mu\text{L/L}$; $C_4 = 0\text{--}10\ \mu\text{L/L}$ (due to PEPCase high affinity).
   - **Saturation Point**: $C_4 \approx 360\ \mu\text{L/L}$; $C_3 \approx 450\ \mu\text{L/L}$. Raising $\text{CO}_2$ enhances $C_3$ crop yields in greenhouses ($\text{CO}_2$ fertilization in tomatoes and bell peppers).
3. **Temperature**: Dark enzymatic reactions are temperature-dependent. $C_4$ plants have a higher optimum ($30\text{--}45^\circ\text{C}$) than $C_3$ plants ($20\text{--}25^\circ\text{C}$).
4. **Water Stress**: Promotes stomatal closure, reduces leaf turgor, and halts $\text{CO}_2$ diffusion.
